# the way of the thread: stream the file into a process of the container (here its /bin/tee) with crictl exec -i
SOCK=/run/bench72228017/containerd.sock
CRI="sudo crictl --runtime-endpoint unix://$SOCK --image-endpoint unix://$SOCK"
ID=$($CRI ps -q --name '^bench72228017-app$' --state running)
PID=$($CRI inspect -o go-template --template '{{.info.pid}}' "$ID")
F=/tmp/bench72228017/test.txt
$CRI exec -i "$ID" /bin/tee /data/test.txt < "$F" > /dev/null

# the root file system of the container as containerd keeps it on the node (the bundle's rootfs), a plain copy
SOCK=/run/bench72228017/containerd.sock
CRI="sudo crictl --runtime-endpoint unix://$SOCK --image-endpoint unix://$SOCK"
ID=$($CRI ps -q --name '^bench72228017-app$' --state running)
PID=$($CRI inspect -o go-template --template '{{.info.pid}}' "$ID")
F=/tmp/bench72228017/test.txt
sudo cp "$F" "/run/bench72228017/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/k8s.io/$ID/rootfs/data/test.txt"

# a bind mount made on the node, on the container's directory in the bundle: the node sees the file there, the container's own mount namespace never gets the mount
SOCK=/run/bench72228017/containerd.sock
CRI="sudo crictl --runtime-endpoint unix://$SOCK --image-endpoint unix://$SOCK"
ID=$($CRI ps -q --name '^bench72228017-app$' --state running)
PID=$($CRI inspect -o go-template --template '{{.info.pid}}' "$ID")
F=/tmp/bench72228017/test.txt
sudo mount --bind /tmp/bench72228017 "/run/bench72228017/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/k8s.io/$ID/rootfs/data"

# only the first 100000 bytes are copied
SOCK=/run/bench72228017/containerd.sock
CRI="sudo crictl --runtime-endpoint unix://$SOCK --image-endpoint unix://$SOCK"
ID=$($CRI ps -q --name '^bench72228017-app$' --state running)
PID=$($CRI inspect -o go-template --template '{{.info.pid}}' "$ID")
F=/tmp/bench72228017/test.txt
sudo sh -c "head -c 100000 \"$F\" > /proc/$PID/root/data/test.txt"

# the container is removed and created again with the host file mounted at /data/test.txt: a different container, a different process
SOCK=/run/bench72228017/containerd.sock
CRI="sudo crictl --runtime-endpoint unix://$SOCK --image-endpoint unix://$SOCK"
ID=$($CRI ps -q --name '^bench72228017-app$' --state running)
PID=$($CRI inspect -o go-template --template '{{.info.pid}}' "$ID")
F=/tmp/bench72228017/test.txt
POD=$(cat /tmp/bench72228017/.bench/pod_id)
python3 - <<'EOF'
import json
c = json.load(open("/tmp/bench72228017/bench72228017-app.json"))
c["mounts"] = [{"container_path": "/data/test.txt", "host_path": "/tmp/bench72228017/test.txt", "readonly": True}]
json.dump(c, open("/tmp/bench72228017/bench72228017-app-again.json", "w"))
EOF
$CRI stop "$ID" >/dev/null; $CRI rm "$ID" >/dev/null
NEW=$($CRI create "$POD" /tmp/bench72228017/bench72228017-app-again.json /tmp/bench72228017/pod.json)
$CRI start "$NEW"

# the file is put into the (read-only) layer of the image the container is made of, found in its mount table: it becomes part of the image
SOCK=/run/bench72228017/containerd.sock
CRI="sudo crictl --runtime-endpoint unix://$SOCK --image-endpoint unix://$SOCK"
ID=$($CRI ps -q --name '^bench72228017-app$' --state running)
PID=$($CRI inspect -o go-template --template '{{.info.pid}}' "$ID")
F=/tmp/bench72228017/test.txt
LOWER=$(sudo awk '$5=="/" {print $NF; exit}' /proc/$PID/mountinfo | sed -n 's/.*lowerdir=\([^,:]*\).*/\1/p')
sudo cp "$F" "$LOWER/data/test.txt"
